ORDER This is the petition filed by the petitioner against the respondents under section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act., 2005 (herein after referred as P.W.D.V. Act, 2005) seeking various relief.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners case is as follows; The marriage of the 1st petitioner with the 1st respondent was solemnized on 10.10.2005 at Sri Jayasurya Kalyana Mantapa, Bylappanapalya,
Tumkur road, Bengaluru as per Hindu customs and rituals in the presence of relatives, friends and well wishers.

It is the submission of petitioner No.1 that, at the time of marriage, the respondent No.1 was working as driver on temporary basis in Revenue Department and he was earning Rs.12,500/- per month, and the respondents demanded dowry and gold ornaments from the petitioner and the same as been fulfilled by her father and he has performed marriage by spending Rs.10,00,000/-.
After the marriage, the petitioner started to reside with her in-laws.
3. The petitioner further submits that, her sister-in-law one Hemavathi is a spinster and she used to reside with the respondent and his parents.
The said Hemavathi used to control whole family and both the respondents used to give their earnings to her.
According to petitioner, the said Hemavathi used to give some meager amount to the petitioner out of which the petitioner has to manage the whole house.
Hence, within 4 months of marriage, the petitioner became very weak and when the 1st respondent question the same, the petitioner informed the 1st respondent about the problem,
hence when the 1st respondent questioned the same to the Hemavathi, she threatened the 1st petitioner and 1st respondent to leave the house stating or else she will commit suicide.

For which,
the mother-in-law of the petitioner has also supported to the said Hemavathi, therefore the 1st respondent moved out of the house and took a separate rental house at Pattegarapalya and it is the father of the petitioner who had helped the 1st respondent financially and maintained both the 1st petitioner and 1st respondent.
4. The petitioner further submits that, during the said period, the 2nd petitioner was born and the delivery expenses were borne by the parents of the petitioner.

According to petitioner, after making separate house, respondent started to consume more and more alcohol, and after delivery when she was at her parent's house and one day, the 1st respondent shifted all the house hold articles and dumped the same before the house of her parents and took the advance amount to utilize the same for his bad habits.

Thereafter, the parents of the petitioner had arranged one more rental house at Chikkabidarakallu by paying Rs.20,000/- towards advance and Rs.2,100/- towards rent, however the respondent failed to pay the rent and it is the parents of the petitioner who looked after both petitioner No.1 and 2, during this period, the 3rd petitioner was born.

5. She further submits that, in September 2009, the 1st respondent informed the 1st petitioner that he has lost his job at Revenue Department and he is working as a driver job in Airport Taxi Service Smt.Deepu @ V. Hence, the petitioner fell unconscious and the same was informed by the neighbors to her parents and her parents came and took her to the hospital wherein she took treatment for 2 days.
6.

The petitioner further submits that, after the incident, she and her parents went to police station and lodged complaint against the respondent, hence, one of the relative of the 1st respondent came to the police station and requested the 1st petitioner and her parents not to lodge complaint and in that panchayath, the 1st respondent asked apologized and assured that he will not commit any offence in future.
Similarly, the 2nd respondent also undertook to retrieve the pledged gold ornaments by the 1st respondent and also to buy a taxi to the 1st respondent, however they did not kept their promise.
The petitioner further submits that, 1st respondent started to force her to act in blue films telling that, he has foreign clients and if she act nobody will know about the same.

7. According to petitioner, the respondent used to stay away from house days together and whenever he returns he used to suspect her character.
She further submits that, 1st respondent used to mix DDT powder and his urine to the drinking water of the petitioners.

The respondent No.1 also failed to admitted the 2nd petitioner to the school and when petitioner No.1 informed the same to the 2nd respondent, the 2nd respondent assured that he will admit the 2nd petitioner to the school
, however he did not kept his words.
Hence, father of the petitioner No.1 admitted the 2nd petitioner to the school by paying all the school fees.

She further submits that, she is a housewife and has no income and both the petitioner and her children are depending upon her parents.

On the other hand, the 1st respondent is working as a driver at Airport Taxi Service and earning salary of more than Rs.10,000/- and 1st respondent and his sister Hemavathi are holding petitioners gold jewelleries worth Rs.2,50,000/- which belongs to the petitioners.
Hence, the petition.
10. After the registration of the petition, notice has been issued to the respondents through RPAD and P.O.
After the service of said notice, 1st respondent appeared before the court and filed his objection to the main petition.
In his objection, respondent except admitting 1st petitioner's marriage with him denied all other allegations.
It is the contention of the respondent that, at the time of marriage, he never demanded dowry or has taken dowry from the petitioner.

According to respondent, petitioner and her parents belongs to poor family and he has helped them and never taken help from them, even at the time of delivery, it is him who has met medical expenses of the petitioner and after marriage, the petitioner only stayed for 45 days in his parents house, thereafter she started to harass him for separate house,
when his family members were unable to bear the torture, they asked him to arrange a separate house, hence they moved to a rented house which was situated nearer to her parent's house and stayed their for 6 month, thereafter, they again shifted their house to another house which was also situated nearer to the house of petitioner.

According to respondent, petitioner is making false allegations against his mother and sister, his sister is married and he had only meager salary of Rs.2,000/- to Rs.2,500/- and he never handed over his salary to his sister.

The respondent further submits that, at the instigation of her father, petitioner is making false allegations against him and they have a relative by name Krishnappa, who is working as a P.C in Bengaluru Police Station and as per his advise, they have drafted the complaint against the respondent for the allegation of dowry harassment.

According to respondent, on 21.11.2011, his father-in-law and brother-in-law by name Gururaj has beaten him and has caused grievous injuries, when the police arrived at the spot, they took the 1st respondent to the hospital and got him treated, thereafter they produced him before Jurisdictional Magistrate and a case was registered and without any fault, he was sent to judicial custody, due to the false complaint of the petitioner, which has caused mental agony to him.

He further submits that, he has no friend by name William and all the allegations made by the petitioner are false, he never suspected her character and till today, he is ready to look after the petitioner and his children, if she rejoins him by forging her illegal acts.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

respondent in their defence examined respondent as RW.1 and got 4 documents marked as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.

sentences.text: 12. Perused both documentary and oral evidence available on record.
Heard arguments.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the relief's sought by her?
3. What order?
16. In the present petition, respondent did not disputed his relationship with the complainant and factum of living together in the shared household prior to their separation.
Accordingly, domestic relationship between the parties as defined under section 2(f) of the P.W.D.V. Act, 2005 is proved.

In order to grant relief under the provision of P.W.D.V. Act, 2005., it is incumbent on the part of the petitioner to prove that she has been subjected to domestic violence by the respondent and she is an aggrieved person as per the provisions of the said act.

17. In order to prove her case, the petitioner No.1 got herself examined as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of examination-in-chief, wherein she reiterated her averments of the petition and it is her contention that, at the time of marriage, the respondents have demanded dowry and gold ornaments and the same as been fulfilled by her father and he has performed marriage by spending Rs.10,00,000/-.
According to petitioner, the respondents have lied about the job of the respondent.

In order to prove her contention, the petitioner got her father examined as PW.2 and the PW.2 filed affidavit in lieu of his examination-in-chief and supported the contention of dowry and marriage expenses of the petitioner.
On the other hand, respondent got himself examined as RW.1 and denied the allegations of dowry and marriage expenses.
In order to prove her contention, petitioner has produced a photograph of the respondent and got that marked as Ex.P.5.
On perusal of the same, it can be seen that, some one is tying something to the hand of respondent.
She has also produced two documents and got them marked as Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.8 respectively.
On perusal of the same, Ex.P.2 is a cash credit bill and it does not contain the name of the purchaser.
Further, date of the bill is 11.08.2006 and as per the contention of the petitioner, her marriage was solemnized on 10.10.2005.

sentences.text: Further, on perusal of Ex.P.8, it is an estimation and no purchase bill has been produced by the petitioner.

With respect to marriage expenses, she has produced a document which she claims to be given by one Lakshmi Provision Store and got that marked as Ex.P.11, the said document is in hand writing and it contains only seal, hence based upon said document, it cannot be said that, the petitioner has spent the shown amount towards catering.
Further, Ex.P.12 and Ex.P.13 are also an estimations and no relative bill has been produced.

Apart from all these things, during the cross-examination of PW.1 dated 26.10.2013, the PW.1 deposes that, she has no information as to who was hired for catering and how much amount has been spent on it and during the cross-examination of PW.2 dated 21.03.2014, he deposes that, he has no documents to prove that,
he has given money to the respondent.

Further, as the alleged incident have alleged to taken place prior to the marriage of petitioner and respondent, at that time, there existed no shared household and domestic relationship between the parties.

In Vijay Verma Vs. State (NCT) of Delhi and another., reported in AIR 2011 (NOC) 171 (DEL), the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi held that, "the purpose of the Act is to give remedy to the aggrieved persons against domestic violence.

entities.text: Vijay Verma Vs. State (NCT) of Delhi and another., reported in AIR 2011 (NOC) 171 (DEL)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The domestic violence can take place only when one is living in shared household with the respondents.
The acts of abuses, emotional or economic, physical or sexual, verbal or nonverbal if committed when one is living in the same shared household constitute domestic violence.
However, such acts of violence can be committed even otherwise also when one is living separate.

When such acts of violence take place when one is living separate, these may be punishable under different provisions of IPC or other penal laws, but, they cannot be covered under Domestic Violence Act".

Hence, the above allegations are not covered under P.W.D.V. Act, 2005.
18.

The petitioner further contended that, the mother of the respondent is a drunkard and respondent used to give all his earnings to his sister by name Hemavathi, who is a spinster and the said Hemavathi did not provided proper food to the petitioner, hence the health of the petitioner deteriorated.
Further, according to petitioner, the said Hemavathi and her parents came to her house during November - 2010 and after mixing some intoxicating chemicals, have stolen all her gold ornaments.
However, during the cross-examination of PW.1 dated 06.09.2013, the petitioner admits the suggestion that, sister of the respondent has been married and she is residing at her husband's house.
Further, according to petitioners own submission, she resided with her in-laws only for 2 to 3 months, thereafter she and respondent moved to a separate house.
After the separation, she never resided with either respondent No.2 or with other in-laws.
She further admits the suggestion that, the 2nd rented house was 25 kilo meter away from the house of 2nd respondent.

Hence, as per the submission of petitioner, after 2 to 3 months of her marriage, she and 1st respondent moved to separate house i.e., in the year 2005 and the present petition has been filed in the year 2012.

In spite of having no shared household between herself and 2nd respondent and even though the sister of the respondent is residing at her husband's house, the petitioner makes vague allegations against them.

Further, though the petitioner claims that, her sister-in-law and parent-in-laws have taken her jewellaries weighing around 180 grams by mixing some intoxicating thing to her food, she files no complaint, in that regard.
If the allegation was true, she would have filed the complaint.
In view of above observation, it clearly goes to show that, the petitioner did not approached this court with clean hands.

Further, during her cross-examination dated 26.10.2013,
when it has been suggested that, after leaving her in-laws house, she never went back to their house,
the witness claims that, after the operation of her father-in-law, she had been there for once to see Smt.Deepu @ V. Lakshmidevi vs H.Manjunath on 20 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29006526/
6

him. That, itself goes to show that, there exist no shared household and domestic relationship and in the absence of shared household and domestic relationship, she is not entitled to claim any relief against 2nd respondent.
19. The petitioner further contends that, the respondent No.1 failed to provide basic necessities and also failed to pay the rent of the rented premises.

According to petitioner, when the respondent lost his job at Revenue Department, he asked petitioner to bring money to buy a second hand taxi, when she refused and asked him to get money from his father, he assaulted petitioner and her children and stole a gold chain from the house and ran away.

Hence, she approached jurisdictional police,
wherein after panchayath, the 1st respondent appolized and assured that, he will not commit any offence in future.
According to petitioner, 2nd respondent assured to retrieve the gold ornaments pledged by 1st respondent and to handover the same to petitioner and also to buy a taxi.
During her cross-examination dated 26.10.2013, the witness deposes that, she has lodged complaint against the respondent.

In the complaint, petitioner has alleged that, the respondent is demanding jewellary and on her failure, he is asking to divorce him, which is in contradiction with the allegations made by the petitioner in her affidavit.
Thereafter, witness denies the suggestion that, on 21.11.2011, her brother and father have assaulted the respondent, hence he has sustained injuries.

Thereafter, when it has been suggested that, due to the injuries the respondent has taken treatment, the witness claims that, when the respondent was assaulting her father, a stone touched him, hence he sustained injuries.
The above admission is in support of the contention of the respondent that, the parents and brother of the petitioner has assaulted him and lodged false complaint against him.
20. The petitioner further contends that, the respondent used to force her to act in blue films and used to sexually abuse her.
According to petitioner, he used to mix DDT powder and his urine to the drinking water of the petitioners.
During her cross-examination dated 26.10.2013, the witness deposes that, she has not lodged any complaint against the respondent stating that, he is forcing her to act in blue films.

Further, according to petitioner, in her unconsciousness state, she does not know, as to what respondent did to her and PW.2 supports her contention, however being father of petitioner, obviously he will support the allegations of the petitioner and
in the absence of complaint and corroborative material, only based upon vague allegations of presumption and hearsay witness,
it can
not be
concluded that, the respondent used to force the petitioner to act in blue films.

According to petitioner, she has not seen person by name William and during her cross- examination dated 26.10.2013, the petitioner claims that, she does not know as to where the respondent is working and names of his friends.

21. The petitioner though has contended that, the respondent tried to ignite her by pouring diesel in the month of November and her neighbor had called Hoysala Police, still no complaint was filed against the respondent on the said day.

According to petitioner, after vacating the house, when she moved to her father's house, the respondent came near her father's house along with some anti social elements and assaulted her father, then she lodged complaint against him.

On the other hand,
it is the contention of the respondent that, petitioner has a relative by name Krishnappa who is working as a P.C. in Bengaluru Police Station and as per his advise, the petitioner drafted complaint by making false allegations of dowry harassment against him and on 21.11.2011, petitioner's father and brother assaulted him and caused grievous injuries to him and on the same day, he was arrested Smt.Deepu @ V. Lakshmidevi vs H.Manjunath on 20 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29006526/
7
due to the false complaint of the petitioner.

During her cross-examination, petitioner admits the suggestion that, her relative by name Krishnappa is working in Police Department and in the petition, no where the petitioner has stated that, on 21.11.2011, respondent has sustained injures,
however during her cross- examination, she claims that, when the respondent tried to assault her father by stone, he sustained injuries.

In view of above observation, the petition fails to prove physical and sexual abuse by the respondent No.1.
22.
With respect to economic abuse, during his cross- examination, though the respondent has claimed that, it is him who was paying rent of the house, he does not know the name of owner of the house.
Further, he does not remember date of birth of his children, he does not know as to in which school, they are studying and claims that, children's are with petitioner and her parents.
He further deposes that, he does not know how much is the education expenses and other expenses of his children and it is the father of the petitioner, who is taking care of it.

The witness further deposes that, he has no documents to prove that, he has provided treatment to petitioner, though he denies the suggestion that, it was her father who has borne medical expenses of the petitioner during her pregnancy.

Further, according to him, out of his money, parents of the petitioner have purchased a property in her name, however he does not remember as to in which year and from whom, the said property has been purchased.
He further admits the suggestion that, from the date of his arrest, he has not given any maintenance to petitioner and her children.

In view of above observation,
economic abuse stands proved.

However, during her cross- examination, petitioner herself has stated that, respondent knows only driving and at present, she has no knowledge as to where he is working, hence having regard to standard of living of respondent, this court is of the considered view that, awarding compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- to the 1st petitioner, is just meet the ends of justice
Hence, I answered both Point No.1 and 2 in the PARTLY AFFIRMATIVE.
23. Point No.3:
For the foregoing discussion and finding on Point No.1 and 2, following order is passed;
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner under section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act., 2005 is hereby Partly allowed.

Accordingly, domestic relationship between the parties as defined under section 2(f) of the P.W.D.V. Act, 2005 is proved.
In order to grant relief under the provision of P.W.D.V. Act, 2005., it is incumbent on the part of the petitioner to prove that she has been subjected to domestic violence by the respondent and she is an aggrieved person as per the provisions of the said act.
